_meta.note: N-D-C values derived from public source research using formulas: balance=100-(|D-C|/max(D,C))*100; N=sqrt(D*C)*(balance/100); sustainability=100/((|D-C|^2)+10). All values PROVISIONAL pending independent phase audit. This project models the Bristol One City urban policy delivery chain, not a physical commodity supply chain. D represents the definition, constraints, and governance requirements of each delivery phase; C represents the actual contribution, measurable output, and delivery achieved.

synthetic.description: Baseline N-D-C values derived from public Bristol One City data, City Leap KPIs, QoL survey, and BCAI reporting. See _meta.sources for citations. All values PROVISIONAL.

phase_meta.name: Vision and Mandate
phase_meta.transformation: Political commitment + civic consultation -> published 2050 vision with 4 missions and SDG mapping

phase_meta.name: Governance and Coordination
phase_meta.transformation: 7 thematic boards + Governance Board -> coordinated partner action across public, private, and voluntary sectors

phase_meta.name: Strategy and Program Design
phase_meta.transformation: Board mandates + BACCC recommendations -> binding delivery strategies (City Leap, Climate Strategy, LNRS, BCAI)

phase_meta.name: Capital Deployment
phase_meta.transformation: Treasury borrowing + private JV investment + citizen investment -> deployed capital in green infrastructure and services

phase_meta.name: Infrastructure Delivery
phase_meta.transformation: Deployed capital -> installed low-carbon assets (heat networks, solar, retrofit, EV charging, LED lighting)

phase_meta.name: Community and Household Uptake
phase_meta.transformation: Installed infrastructure + community programs -> household behaviour change, deprived-community benefit, scope 3 reduction

phase_meta.name: Outcome Measurement
phase_meta.transformation: City-wide data collection -> independently verified progress against 2030 carbon target, QoL indicators, and SDG commitments

0.notes: Highest D in chain. Five iterations of One City Plan (2019-2025); binding 2030 carbon neutral target (scope 1/2/3); 4 missions mapped to 17 UN SDGs; BACCC independent advisory; 200+ stakeholder consultation for 2025 revision. C gap: plan has no legally binding enforcement mechanism; progress against social equity missions is not legally compelled.
0.scope_source: City-wide scope 1/2/3 baseline established by Arup/CSE 2020; city CO2 down 43% since 2005 baseline

1.notes: 7 thematic boards plus Governance Board (12 members drawn from anchor institutions). Co-chair structure (one councillor, one external per board) ensures cross-sector legitimacy. BACCC acts as independent critical friend. C gap: inter-board integration is new (missions launched Oct 2024); board strategies not consistently co-produced with communities; cross-board data sharing limited.

1.scope_source: Governance does not directly produce measurable carbon outputs

2.notes: Best-defined phase. City Leap has legally binding contractual KPIs (140,000t carbon savings, 180MW zero-carbon generation, 327GWh generated, £61.5m social value). BCAI has a published Green Finance Framework. LNRS published November 2024. C near-match: IBP signed and all major strategies published. Minor C gap: LNRS criticism (focus areas not covering most development sites); social equity strategies less binding than environmental.

3.notes: Critical D-C imbalance. D=275 is highest in chain: £1.67bn capital budget (2026-27), PWLB borrowing constraints, City Leap 50/50 JV governance obligations, ICMA Green Finance Framework requirements. C=195: BCAI has only raised ~£2m (target £2m initial phase, institutional market untapped); City Leap at approximately 48% of social value KPI midway through 5-year term; scope 3 capital mobilisation essentially zero. The gap between available governance frameworks and actual capital mobilised defines the primary structural bottleneck above Phase 5.

4.notes: Good delivery phase. City Leap physical KPIs on track: heat network expanded (award-winning), solar at schools, social housing retrofit underway, LED lighting installed, EV charging rolled out. Mandatory 10% BNG in planning system. Council direct emissions cut 67% since 2015. C gap: IBP forecast requires £631m deployment vs pipeline still being built; community energy fund at £1.5m is small relative to need; scope 2 decarbonisation depends on national grid improvement.

5.notes: PRIMARY BOTTLENECK. D-C gap of 100 points is the largest in the chain. D=240: BNG 10% mandatory, pay-as-you-save model designed, community energy fund established, BCAI accessible from £5. C=140: only 750 retail BCAI investors from a city of 470,000; BNG offsetting market nascent (LNRS coverage gap noted by Bristol Tree Forum Jan 2025); scope 3 emissions (consumption-based) essentially unaddressed; LNRS does not apply to most development sites; 10.7-year life expectancy gap between most and least deprived wards not improving; community energy uptake is early-stage. The gap between institutional ambition and household/community-level delivery is the structural failure of the One City system.

synthetic.interpretation: The Bristol One City delivery chain scores 81.3% overall balance (Good zone), but this aggregate masks a critical structural failure at Phase 5 (Community and Household Uptake, 58.3% — Poor). The system has built exemplary infrastructure at the top of the chain: the One City Plan is well-defined (Phase 0, 88.9%), governance is coordinated (Phase 1, 84.0%), major strategies are contractually grounded (Phase 2, 90.6%), and outcome measurement is robust (Phase 6, 91.9%). However, the gap between institutional ambition and household-level delivery is the defining failure. Capital deployment (Phase 3, 70.9%) is the secondary bottleneck: the city has a £1.67bn capital budget and £1bn City Leap JV but has mobilised only £2m through citizen investment mechanisms. Phase 5's D-C gap of 100 points — where 240 points of D (mandatory requirements, designed programmes) is met by only 140 points of C (actual uptake, community benefit) — represents the structural disconnect between Bristol's ambitious policy commitments and the lived experience of the 53,100 residents in the city's most deprived communities. The 10.7-year male life expectancy gap between most and least deprived wards is the single most visible outcome of sustained Phase 5 failure.
